title: Roast red cabbage bowls with spelt and smoked mackerel

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything here is a whole food or a traditional condiment; horseradish sauce and smoked mackerel are long-standing British larder items.

supermarket.reason: Red cabbage, sprouts, pearled spelt, smoked mackerel, horseradish and Greek yoghurt are all everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a saucepan and a sieve, and the techniques are simple roasting and simmering.

works.reason: Eight cabbage wedges with sprouts at 200°C for 30 minutes, 200g spelt simmered for 25 minutes, and 250g mackerel make a sensible, well-seasoned lunch for four.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers wedging the cabbage, halving 200g of sprouts, dicing an apple and flaking the fish, and the 30-minute roast matches the cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Roast red cabbage is the centre of a warm December lunch bowl, with sprouts and apple alongside it.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling mix of wholegrain, two vegetables, oily fish and yoghurt that a family would happily eat.
